_meta.description: Belt galleries — curated NASA imagery presented as portraits of each belt's largest members. Reuses existing small-body imagery (under static/images/small-bodies/) rather than duplicating files. Caption per slot tells the user which body they're looking at so the gallery reads as a tour of the belt's catalogued giants.

asteroid.caption: Ceres — the largest body in the asteroid belt, photographed by NASA Dawn from its 1,470 km mapping orbit. Diameter ≈ 940 km.
Occator Crater on Ceres — the bright spots are sodium-carbonate salt deposits, evidence of a subsurface brine ocean.
Ahuna Mons on Ceres — a 4-km-tall cryovolcano, the only one yet identified on a dwarf planet.

kuiper.caption: Pluto — New Horizons portrait from 450,000 km, July 2015. Sputnik Planitia (the heart-shaped nitrogen-ice plain) dominates the encounter hemisphere.
Pluto's atmosphere backlit by the Sun — nitrogen haze layers stretching ~200 km above the surface.
Eris — slightly more massive than Pluto. Its 2005 discovery triggered the IAU's 2006 definition of 'dwarf planet'.
Haumea — the most elongated known Kuiper-Belt object. Rapid rotation (3.9 h) stretches it to ≈ 2,322 × 1,704 × 1,026 km.
Makemake — fourth-largest known KBO, surface dominated by methane ice; the only one of the classical-KBO 'big four' with a known moon (S/2015 (136472) 1).
